prompt: What does `server_tokens off` change?
hint: Compare the Server header before and after.

choices.text: Removes the Server header from every response
Fixes the known flaws in that version

prompt: Why is hiding the version worth doing, given that it does not fix anything?
hint: Think of the day a flaw is published.

choices.why: A few bytes fewer change nothing measurable.
Right. It removes the free list.

choices.text: Browsers trust servers that hide versions
choices.why: Browsers do not look at it.
TLS says nothing about the Server header.

prompt: The shop sends `Server: ipe-shop/1.0` on its own port, but responses through Nginx carry Nginx's Server header. Why?
hint: A proxy hides some upstream headers by default.

choices.text: The shop changes its header when proxied
choices.why: The shop does not know it is proxied.
It was already replaced before that setting.

prompt: Before the catch-all block, `curl -k https://127.0.0.1/` returned the bookshop. Why is that a problem?
hint: Who asks by address?

choices.text: It made the whole site noticeably slower
Scanners index it, and other names reach it
It broke the certificate for the real name
choices.why: The certificate was fine for its names.

choices.text: The shop received requests it could not parse at all
choices.why: The shop never saw them; Nginx served the static page.

prompt: What does `return 444` make Nginx do?
hint: curl said `Empty reply from server`.

choices.text: Send a page saying the site is unknown

choices.why: Right. A code of Nginx's own.
The number is just a code.

prompt: Why does the catch-all's HTTPS listener use `ssl_reject_handshake on` instead of a certificate of its own?
hint: What would a certificate tell the stranger?

choices.text: Nginx cannot hold two certificates at once
choices.why: It can have one per server block.
Right. Refusing the handshake shows nothing.

choices.text: Pebble cannot issue a certificate for an IP
choices.why: That is not the reason the lesson gives.

choices.text: It is faster than answering with a 444
choices.why: Both are cheap; the point is what is revealed.

prompt: Match each header to what it tells the browser.
hint: The lesson's table.

pairs.right: use only HTTPS for this name
do not guess the type of a file
load resources only from these places
send only the origin when following a link away

prompt: The redirect on port 80 carries no `Strict-Transport-Security`. Is that a mistake?
hint: What does a browser do with HSTS received over HTTP?

choices.text: Yes; HSTS belongs on every response
Yes; it should be on port 80 only
choices.why: Over HTTP anybody on the path could forge it.

choices.text: No; browsers ignore HSTS sent over HTTP
No; HSTS only works with preload
choices.why: It works on the first HTTPS visit without preload.

prompt: A team sets `max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload` on day one. A month later an old subdomain that serves only HTTP stops working for their users. Why?
hint: What does includeSubDomains cover?

choices.text: Browsers now force HTTPS for every name under the domain, for a year
choices.why: Right. Start short and widen later.
The subdomain never had HTTPS at all.

choices.text: Preload deletes HTTP sites from search engines
choices.why: It is a list inside browsers.

choices.text: max-age is in milliseconds, so it already expired
choices.why: It is in seconds: a year.

prompt: Which page breaks under the bookshop's Content-Security-Policy?
hint: `default-src 'self'` and no `'unsafe-inline'`.

choices.why: A script file from the same site is allowed.
The scheme has nothing to do with it.

prompt: Why is a new CSP introduced first as `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only`?
hint: It enforces nothing.

choices.text: To find what it would break first
Report-only mode is stricter than enforcing
Browsers need a week to learn a new policy
choices.why: They apply it on the next load.

prompt: After `add_header Cache-Control "no-store";` was added to `location /api/`, the API's responses lost HSTS and CSP. Why?
hint: Inheritance of add_header is all or nothing.

choices.text: Cache-Control conflicts with HSTS in browsers
choices.why: Both appeared together after the fix.

choices.text: Proxied responses never carry security headers
choices.why: They did once the snippet was included.
The new header was there, so the reload worked.

prompt: What catches the add_header trap before a visitor does?
hint: Nginx itself reports nothing.

choices.why: The configuration is valid; nothing is wrong syntactically.
The trap is in what the file means, not what it says.

prompt: Why does the dotfile location answer 404 rather than 403?
hint: What does a 403 tell a scanner?

choices.text: A 404 is faster for Nginx to send
403 is not allowed inside a location
Search engines index pages that answer 403

prompt: The dotfile rule is `location ~ /\.(?!well-known/)`. Why the exception?
hint: Lesson 3's renewals.

choices.why: Right. Renewals must still reach them.

choices.text: well-known files are always safe to publish, whatever they contain
choices.why: The exception is for one need, not a blanket trust.

choices.text: Regular expressions cannot match the letter w

choices.why: Git is the thing being hidden.

prompt: With `limit_except GET HEAD PUT { deny all; }`, what does a DELETE to the API get, and from whom?
hint: Before the change it was 405 from the shop.

choices.why: That was before; now it never reaches the shop.
Nothing is deleted, and it is refused.
The request was for the right name.

prompt: `rate=10r/s burst=20 nodelay`: of 60 requests sent back to back, 42 were served. Where do the 42 come from?
hint: A bucket, and a refill.

choices.why: That is a coincidence of numbers, not the mechanism.

choices.text: Each of the four workers allows ten of its own
choices.why: The zone is shared by every worker.

prompt: Why set `limit_req_status 429`?
hint: Nginx's default refusal is another code.

choices.text: 429 is faster for Nginx to send than 503
503 is reserved for TLS handshake errors

prompt: With `client_header_timeout 5s`, after how many seconds did Nginx close a connection whose request never finished?
hint: The `time` output.

prompt: Which endpoint deserves the strictest rate limit, measured in requests per minute?
hint: What does a limit make slow?

choices.why: Right. It is what makes guessing passwords slow.

prompt: Why does Nginx's master process keep running as root while the workers run as www-data?
hint: What needs root?

choices.why: Right. Requests are handled by the workers.

choices.text: To serve requests faster than the workers can
Root is needed to write the access logs

prompt: After the drop-in, `systemd-analyze security` went from 9.2 to 3.6. Which line keeps the shop able to save prices?
hint: Everything else became read-only.

choices.why: That gives a private /tmp, not the database.

prompt: Under `ProtectSystem=strict` with `ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/shop`, even root got `Read-only file system` writing to /opt/shop. What does that protect against?
hint: Assume the layer before has already failed.

choices.text: A slow client holding a connection open
An expired certificate on the site
A broken-into service rewriting its own code
A leaked version number in the Server header field

prompt: Of everything `ss -ltn` listed, which listens on every address?
A new server goes on a public address. Put the hardening steps in a sensible order.
hint: Close the doors before opening the shop.
items: Start Nginx with a catch-all default server
Obtain a certificate and redirect to HTTPS
Add security headers, then test every location
trap: Headers come after HTTPS works, since HSTS is a commitment.

prompt: Which of these should a production response not carry? Choose all that apply.
hint: The checklist at the end of the first section.

choices.text: A version number in Server or X-Powered-By
A stack trace on an error

choices.why: That one belongs on every HTTPS response.

prompt: A security scan reports that `https://203.0.113.20/` shows a login page for an internal tool, though the tool is meant to be reached only as `tools.example.net`. Which change fixes it at the web server?
hint: Which block answers an address?

choices.text: Hide the version number with server_tokens off

choices.why: HSTS does not choose which site answers.
Useful, and the page is still reachable by address.

choices.text: A default server refusing unknown names
